abstract: We investigate when is it beneficial to simultaneously learn representations for several tasks, in low-resource settings. For this, we work with noisy user-generated texts in Algerian, a low-resource non-standardised Arabic variety. That is, to mitigate the problem of the data scarcity, we experiment with jointly learning progressively 4 tasks, namely code-switch detection, named entity recognition, spell normalisation and correction, and identifying users’ sentiments. The selection of these tasks is motivated by the lack of labelled data for automatic morpho-syntactic or semantic sequence-tagging tasks for Algerian, in contrast to the case of much multi-task learning for NLP. Our empirical results show that multi-task learning is beneficial for some tasks in particular settings, and that the effect of each task on another, the order of the tasks, and the size of the training data of the task with more data do matter. Moreover, the data augmentation that we performed with no external resources has been shown to be beneficial for certain tasks.

bibliographic.title: When is Multi-task Learning Beneficial for Low-Resource Noisy Code-switched User-generated Algerian Texts?
bibliographic.venue: Proceedings of the LREC 2020 – 4th Workshop on Computational Approaches to Code Switching

content.problem: It is unclear whether multi-task learning results reported for well-resourced languages generalise to low-resource settings, compounded by the scarcity of labelled data for processing noisy user-generated Algerian Arabic.
content.proposed_solution: The authors jointly train four tasks (code-switch detection, named entity recognition, spelling normalisation and correction, and sentiment analysis) on Algerian user-generated data using a multi-task neural architecture with shared encoders, systematically varying task combinations, task order, word context, training data size, and data augmentation.
content.algorithm_or_model: Multi-task encoder-decoder neural architecture with shared character-level and sequence-level CNN encoders and task-specific decoders
dataset_testbed: Algerian code-switch detection dataset (Adouane and Dobnik, 2017)
Algerian spelling normalisation and correction dataset (Adouane et al., 2019)
Algerian sentiment analysis dataset (Adouane et al., 2020)
New Algerian code-switched NER dataset created by the authors (46,710 comments, 17,133 named entities)

content.claim: Multi-task learning is beneficial for some tasks only in particular settings, with the pairwise choice of tasks, the order of tasks, and the size of the training data of the task with more data all determining whether joint training helps or hurts.

evidence.problem_quote: This paper is an attempt to take advantage of the stateof-the-art advances in NLP, namely deep neural networks (DNNs) and multi-task learning in order to mitigate the problem of the scarcity of labelled data for colloquial Algerian language (henceforth referred to as ALG).
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: To this end, we jointly train 4 tasks (or subsets thereof): (1) Code-Switch Detection (CSD), (2) Named Entity Recognition (NER) —both framed as sequence tagging— and (3) Spelling Normalisation and Correction (SPELL) —framed as a sequence-to-sequence task— and (4) identifying users’ sentiments (SA) —framed as a classification task.
evidence.claim_quote: Our empirical results show that multi-task learning is beneficial for some tasks in particular settings, and that the effect of each task on another, the order of the tasks, and the size of the training data of the task with more data do matter. Moreover, the data augmentation that we performed with no external resources has been shown to be beneficial for certain tasks.
